newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso rebounds due to high rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso rebounds due to high rates.

text.p: * Banks sell dollars to generate peso liquidity
The Philippine peso rallied on Wednesday after two days of declines as banks sold their dollars in view of the high interest rates on the overnight market.
The peso closed at 26.235 to the dollar versus 26.240.
The day's average was 26.232 from 26.244, with turnover rising to $190.20 million from $159.80 million.
"Everyone was expecting the peso to rebound because of the liquidity crunch in the overnight market," said a dealer.
The average interbank call loan rate spiked up to 12.00 percent from 11.71875 after banks loaded themselves with dollars and T-bills in recent days.
The Central Bank stepped in again to smooth out the volatility in the market. It bought some $33.5 to $36 million at rates ranging from 26.231 to 26.235, traders said.
"Obviously, the Central Bank wanted to buy dollars after it sold so much the past few days," a dealer said.
